_provenance: Re-baselined 2026-10-08 for Sol's `129`.5. The System 5 presence decision cited `8.4.4.1.(5); Table 8.4.4.7.-B` as a LITERAL, so a necb2025 run told an authority its AHJ-11 condition came from the other edition's articles. Both branches now derive the citation from the edition's own `reference_subsection`, which is why four per-edition literal counts drop by one each: 2020/8.4.4.1 and 2020/8.4.4.7 cited 5->4 and 6->5, and the 2025 counterparts the same. Nothing is lost from the PRODUCT — the citation is now correct for both editions rather than correct for one — but a literal-only per-edition scanner can no longer see it, which is the same trade every other prefix-derived citation in this file already made. One dynamic key is added, `presence_article`; it is a NAME, so the foreign scanner counts it conservatively rather than inspecting its content, and the unheated branch's inline f-string cites only Section 8.4 articles and so is not foreign at all. Verified end to end in the frozen full-year determination-02 run: the AHJ-11 condition carries '8.4.5.1.(5); Table 8.4.5.7.-B'.

Re-baselined 2026-10-08 for AHJ-10. The corner-block grouping choice was NOT audited — Sol's `127` traced it to `VAVReheat._dominant_orientation`, which has no audit object, while the register claimed it was. The fix is the metadata handoff he specified: the generic builder records structured grouping evidence and learns no NECB ids, and `btap.codes` emits the entry. That entry cites `Table 8.4.x.7.-B Note (3)`, so 2020/8.4.4.7 and 2025/8.4.5.7 each gain one `cited` site: 227 to 229. An ADDITION, not a loss — and it makes D-18 genuinely runtime-wired, so its kind moves from `runtime_unwired` to `runtime`.

Re-baselined 2026-10-08 for Fable's `131` F6, the class Sol's `129`.5 had already called a defect: a 2020 article number written as a LITERAL in action text on a run whose `article=` field was correctly 2025. It reaches an authority, because the resolver quotes the deciding entry's action verbatim as the condition `detail`, and in NECB 2025 the 8.4.4 subsection is archetype EUI entirely. Three citations in reference.py now derive the edition's own prefix instead of spelling 2020's: the D-28 multizone merge decision's `Table 8.4.x.7.-B Note (3)`, and the humidification capture decision and orphan warning's `Table 8.4.x.7.-B Note (1)`. That is why 8.4.4.7 and 8.4.5.7 each drop two `cited` and one `warn`, 229 to 223. Nothing is lost from the PRODUCT — each citation is now right for both editions where it was right for one — but a literal-only per-edition scanner can no longer see it, the same trade the two entries above made. Two more of the same class were fixed outside this file's scope: the heat-pump redirect action (already had `hp_article` computed above it) and efficiency.py's fan-curve warning, whose own comment said "(2025: 8.4.5.17)" while the string said 8.4.4.17. That one was found by sweeping both editions at runtime rather than reported, and the sweep is now a test: a necb2025 run must cite no 8.4.4.x article. The check is deliberately one-way, because NECB 2020 legitimately cites 8.4.5.x for its part-load curve tables.

Re-baselined 2026-10-08 for Fable's `133` G3, which found F6's fix incomplete and its gate's premise false. Five more sites spelled NECB 2020's subsection on every run, and the frozen corpus saw all five while the gate's fixture reached none: the ECONOMIZER decisions' `article` field (`8.4.4.12.; 5.2.2.7.(1)` — and in NECB 2025 `8.4.4.12` does not exist at all, that subsection stops at `.2`), the no-annual branch of the auxiliary-fuel election (F6 fixed three branches; this was the fourth, the one `--simulate none` exercises), three staged heat-pump warnings that ignored the `hp_article` parameter they were already passed, the hydronic pump article in two places, and the compliance-step text naming the lighting and SHW articles. 2020/8.4.4.12 and 2025/8.4.5.12 each drop two `cited`; the others were action text and never counted. `apply_economizer_thresholds` took no code at all, so the edition is now threaded from the pipeline. Nothing is lost from the product: each citation is right for both editions where it was right for one.

Re-baselined 2026-10-08 for issue #72, and this one is an INCREASE where the last two were losses. The scanner found citations by literal text and understood exactly ONE interpolated name, `prefix`, so resolving an article through any other variable made it invisible — and resolving through the manifest is the project's stated direction for per-edition correctness. The two entries above this one recorded exactly that trade, twice, as citations got MORE correct and the coverage document got quieter. #72 predicted it would recur on every such fix. The scanner now resolves a name bound to `<x>.article("key")` or to a subsection helper, including a two-step binding built from another, and `article=<call>` with no f-string around it. Ten sites come back: the economizer pair, the humidification Note (1) pair, the heat-pump redirect, and the direct-lookup sites in the selection tables. Not resolved, deliberately: a name bound from a parameter, a subscript or a conditional, which needs interprocedural analysis to be correct — and a wrong attribution is worse than a missing one, so the remainder is COUNTED by test_coverage_citation_visibility rather than guessed at.
